title: Quantization hysteresis and batch interplay: long-warmup FP8/INT8 throughput & tail-latency study
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: Recent calibration runs for FP8/INT8 variants show non-monotonic throughput and tail-latency when we vary batch size and long-context windows. We suspect hysteresis in kernel selection + KV-cache warmup creates transient regions where inferred latency spikes and throughput reduces for a sustained period (tens of seconds) after a burst. Goal: produce reproducible microbenchmarks and end-to-end harness results that characterize (1) steady-state throughput across batch sizes and sequence lengths, (2) transient tail-latency after microbursts (warmup), and (3) points where kernel fallback triggers and causes accuracy/perf trade-offs. The results will feed a mitigation plan (runtime heuristics, calibration policy changes, and an autoscaler tuning doc).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmark harness that can run FP8 and INT8 artifacts with identical prompts and record token-level latency and accuracy metrics
Heatmaps for throughput and p95/p99 latency across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32] and sequence lengths [256,1024,2048,4096] for both quant formats
A short list of kernel-fallback thresholds (seq length, batch, kv-cache-hit rate) where fallback occurs
Identified hysteresis windows: time-to-steady-state after a microburst for each config, measured on dedicated GPU pools
Actionable recommendations: at least 3 runtime changes or calibration workflow updates with estimated impact on cost/latency and a proposed rollout plan
tasks: Design harness using existing perf-bench infra but extend to record kernel selection traces and KV-cache hit/miss counters
Create calibration manifests for FP8 and INT8 variants (narrow/standard/wide quant profiles) and lock seeds for repeated runs
Run grid sweep: batch x seq-length x kv-cache-warmup (cold, warm-10s, warm-30s, prefilled) on dedicated-qa cluster
Instrument runtime to emit timestamped kernel IDs and fallback reasons into perf traces
Validate accuracy delta for each quant variant against fp32 baseline using eval prompts (statistical significance check)
Collate results into a single dashboard and produce heatmaps + time-series of post-burst tail-latency
Draft mitigation doc and PRs for runtime heuristics (kernel hysteresis damping, prefill policy, and adaptive batching cap)
Share interim findings with PM and research for next prioritization cadence
decisions: Focus on two quant profiles: FP8 (e4m3-like profile) and INT8 symmetric with per-channel scaling — other profiles deferred
Use dedicated-qa to avoid noisy noisy-hosted interference and to measure invariant kernel behavior
Accuracy validation will use our canonical eval-suite (200 prompt pairs) and report ROUGE/ExactMatch + average embedding cosine similarity
Initial mitigation will be runtime-only; if accuracy regression > 0.6% absolute we will add calibration re-run step to pipeline
experiments: EXP-01: Cold vs Warm KV-cache — run 1000 short requests, then 200 steady requests; measure p95/p99 over time
EXP-02: Batch ramp — step batch size from 1 to 32 mid-traffic and record kernel fallback events
EXP-03: Long context saturation — run 4096-token windows with intermittent bursts to observe sustained memory pressure and fallback
EXP-04: Calibration sensitivity — compare calibration datasets (random prompts vs domain prompts) impact on accuracy under INT8
EXP-05: Autoscaler interaction — run batching with autoscaler configured at different thresholds to observe oscillation/hysteresis
artifacts: Runtime traces: s3://redwood-perf/ENG-261001/traces/ (s3 listing in dashboard)
notes: Early runs show an unexpected kernel selection flip when batch >= 8 and seq >= 2048; fallback adds ~40ms/token in the critical path
FP8 shows slightly higher p95 but lower throughput vs INT8 in warm-cache steady-state for long sequences — likely due to different kernel memory layouts
Calibration artifacts were re-used from ENG-24083; we flagged that set as potentially leading to overfitting to short contexts
